reason: A panicle of racemes is a panicle, so PO panicle inflorescence is the right part. That its last branches are racemes is a detail the source words keep. The rule 'panicled' (R0151) also maps to this class.
PO shoot-borne root has 'aerial root' as a synonym. Rootlets are small aerial roots, which is a narrower case of the same class. Size is a quality and does not need its own bearer.

PO septum (PO_0000030) is defined as a partition formed by fused organ walls, such as ovary or anther walls. A 'cloison' in a stem or pith (a diaphragm) does not fit, so limit the rule to ovary, fruit and anther contexts.
Plural of cloison. Same limit as R3239: PO septum is the partition of a fused ovary, fruit or anther cavity.

The accepted rules 'glandular spot(s)' (R3030, R3033) and 'gland dot(s)' (R2739–R2742) already map to this class, following C265 (gland -> portion of secretory tissue). The surface quality is FLOPO gland-dotted (FLOPO:0991174), handled separately. French 'taches glanduleuses' is the same thing.
Same as R3241: glandular macules are flat glands seen as spots, like the accepted 'glandular spots' rules.

This matches the accepted rules 'pellucid dots' (R3043) and 'pellucid gland' (R3245). Pellucid dots in leaves, petals and sepals are oil cavities, and PO oil gland has 'oil cavity' as a synonym. A part constraint would only drop valid perianth uses, and 'rutaceae' is a family, not a part.
French for pellucid dots. Same as R3243 and R3043.

This follows C270 and the accepted rules 'veinlets' (R2697) and 'nerville' (R2624), which map to leaf lamina vein, the parent of all leaf vein orders. Almost all uses are about leaf veins. A rule for perianth veins would need phyllome lamina vein (PO_0025348) across the whole veinlet family, not this one word.
Plural of veinule. Same as R3254.

'Culm' is a PO synonym of stem, and PO cauline leaf is 'a vascular leaf borne on the stem', so a culm leaf is a narrower cauline leaf. Its sheath is already covered: 'culm sheath' maps to leaf sheath (R2449). 'Culm leave' is a word form from 'culm leaves', not a different term.
Same as R3257: a leaf borne on the culm (stem) is a cauline leaf by PO's own definition.
Plural of culm leaf. Same as R3257.

A bare 'sinker' is ambiguous: in mistletoes (Loranthaceae, Viscaceae) it is the feeding organ that grows into the host (a haustorium), not a root, and elsewhere it is a descending root. No single class fits.

A sinker root is a vertical root that grows down from a lateral root. PO has no narrower class, and mapping a narrower name to its PO parent is the normal pattern for bearer rules ('Narrower: ...'). PO root is correct, just less specific.
Plural of sinker root. Same as R3261.
Plural of the ambiguous bare 'sinker' (mistletoe feeding organ or root). Same as R3260.
'Bole' is already an exact PO synonym of stem (along with 'trunk'). Flora texts use it only for a tree trunk, so no constraint is needed.

This follows the accepted rules 'resin gland(s)' (R2721, R2722) and 'gland dot(s)' (R2739–R2742), which map to portion of secretory tissue (C265). It is not resin canal (PO_0005665), which is a duct. The dotted surface is the separate value gland-dotted.
Same as R3267.
Same as R3267, written with a space.

A panicled cyme is a branched (panicle-like) group of cymes, close to a thyrse. As a whole it is not a PO cyme inflorescence. PO splits thyrse into determinate and indeterminate classes, and earlier reviews used the value thyrse-like (FLOPO:0991199) for that reason. No bearer rule fits safely.
Same as R3270.

PO has no sporangiophore class. PO sporophyll is 'a leaf-like organ bearing sporangia', but the stalked, shield-shaped (peltate) sporangiophores of Equisetum are not clearly leaf-like, and in fungi the word means something else. Leave unmapped or ask for a new class.
Plural of sporangiophore. Same as R3272.

In floras, 'secondary venation' carries counts and patterns of the secondary veins ('6–8 pairs', 'brochidodromous'). These are qualities of the secondary veins as a set, so PO secondary leaf vein is the right part for them.

'Costal vein' is ambiguous. In ferns it is a vein along the costa (the midrib of a pinna, sometimes forming small closed areas), and elsewhere it is a vein near the midrib or margin. It is not reliably a secondary vein, and no single PO class fits.
Plural of costal vein. Same as R3279.

PO second order inflorescence axis has the synonym 'first order inflorescence branch', so the rule works for inflorescences. On a tree or shoot, a first-order branch is PO branch, so limit the rule to inflorescence contexts.
Plural of first-order branch. Same as R3281.
